analysis:
Examined StartCommand+Modes.swift base and head: the only change is the .quarantined message at line 413, now "quarantined on this Mac" instead of "after failed starts". It is cosmetic, and the auto-update gating, exec and quarantine handling are unchanged. UpdateCommand.swift adds `--rollback` and `--yes` flags plus `validate()` (lines 44-57). `--rollback` is rejected with --check-only, --override-quarantine and --coordinator, and `--yes` is rejected without `--rollback`. `run()` at lines 69-76 delegates to the new `UpdateRollback(...).run(skipConfirmation: yes)` and returns before any network update path. The other UpdateCommand edits are help and warning strings. Coordinator URL override is disallowed in rollback mode, so no new coordinator trust input is added in the visible code.

Limit: the body of the added provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/UpdateRollback.swift (173 lines) was not supplied as text. Only a truncated patch excerpt was given, showing the Host struct, the cluster refusal and the doc comment. Its security properties are therefore unverified. The relevant threat model is T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable provider binary), T-047 (downgrade or stale provider keeps privileged fan control), T-053/T-054 (stale or revoked build accepted), T-013 (binary replacement) and A-017/A-011 (build qualification and binary hash registry).

Questions for the next pass:
(1) Does `SelfUpdater.rollBackToPredecessor` re-verify the predecessor's hash, signature and qualification, or does it trust the on-disk copy?
(2) Can a rollback land on a release revoked by the coordinator or App Attest qualification? Registration should still fail closed in that case.
(3) Is the drain-held update lease respected so that rollback does not race the watchdog or an auto-update?
(4) Does the fan helper lease get released across the swap?
(5) Does the quarantine written by rollback stop auto-update from silently reinstalling the release?

No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
